messages:
jessica-support: Heads up — enterprise customer hitting partial chat output when using SSE through their corp proxy. Response stops mid-sentence; final event never arrives. Customer provided request id rq_1a2b3c4d. Can we collect repro steps?
ryan-infra: Thx. Do we know what proxy stack they're on (nginx/iis/zscaler/Palo Alto)? Any curl repro already attempted?
maria-ops: They report 'BlueGate' corporate proxy + Palo Alto. Tried our JS streaming client (EventSource) from their intranet and got first ~200 tokens then silence. No full final event.
jessica-support: Asked them to run a minimal curl to show raw SSE behaviour. Sent this example (note `-N` to disable curl buffering):

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-xxx" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: rq_1a2b3c4d" -d '{"model":"redwood-1f","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \n  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream" -v
```

samir-eng: Good — also ask them to try `--http1.1` (or `--no-http2`) in case HTTP/2 proxy multiplexing is coalescing frames. `-N` is correct for no-buffer.
ryan-infra: Also capture response headers from curl -v. We need `Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Type`, and any `Via`/proxy headers. If upstream proxy is buffering, it may coalesce SSE chunks until buffer fills. Nginx has `proxy_buffering on` by default which causes this.
jessica-support: Server side logs for rq_1a2b3c4d show: 

```
[2026-03-15T18:12:03Z] rq_1a2b3c4d STREAM_OPEN client=10.2.34.5
[2026-03-15T18:12:03Z] rq_1a2b3c4d STREAM_CHUNK size=128 flush=1
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] rq_1a2b3c4d STREAM_CHUNK size=256 flush=0
[2026-03-15T18:12:10Z] rq_1a2b3c4d STREAM_EOF missing-final-flush
```

samir-eng: That looks like we flushed an initial chunk then later chunks didn't flush. Strong signal of proxy coalescing. Ask them to test a direct connection (bypass proxy) to confirm; if they can't, request their proxy config (nginx `proxy_buffering`/`proxy_max_temp_file_size` or corporate appliance settings). Also request a pcap of the session if possible.
maria-ops: Customer says they cannot bypass proxy. They provided some headers: `Via: BlueGate/2.1`, `X-Proxy-Timeout: 60s`, and their frontend times out at 30s. I'll ask for the proxy config (PAC file / nginx conf snippet) and a HAR from browser, plus `curl -N -v` output.
ryan-infra: For our repro bundle ask them to send:
- `curl -N -v` output (both stdout and stderr)
- HAR / browser net logs (Chrome export)
- Any proxy config / PAC file or nginx snippet
- pcap/tcpdump of the session if allowed
- The exact `X-Request-ID` header we gave (rq_1a2b3c4d)
Also ask them to try the websocket fallback: `wss://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/ws` to see if WS avoids buffering.
jessica-support: Sent the checklist. Also requested they try `curl -N --http1.1` and `curl -N --no-buffer` to confirm. Noted to include full timestamps.
samir-eng: If proxy is the culprit, we can add an SSE heartbeat (comment line `:\n`) every 5s to force flush on our side as an interim. I'll prototype an instrumentation flag to enable periodic keepalive comments for affected requests.
deploy-bot: Trace created: trace-id tr_7890fedc for rq_1a2b3c4d. Added to infra triage.
ryan-infra: One more suggestion — some corporate proxies mishandle HTTP/2 push and will buffer until stream end or FIN. `--http1.1` test is important. Also `nghttp` client or `h2load` can help.
jessica-support: Customer will run tests and share logs/pcap today. I'll post updates here when they come in. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
